purpose: T2.1 experiment: does a particle-aware load-balance work estimate reduce FOGGIE's imbalance?

config.note: 4 arms run CONCURRENTLY on separate nodes, so time-varying node conditions are controlled; node scatter is ~1.6% against effects of 65-196%.

verdict: DECISIVE NEGATIVE. Particle-weighted balancing makes FOGGIE monotonically WORSE: +65% wall at weight 1, +196% at weight 100. Keep LoadBalanceParticleWeight = 0 (the default).

mechanism.evidence: Total ChemistryCooling work is essentially CONSTANT across arms (192.0, 188.8, 192.1, 192.7 s) while its max/mean skew explodes (2.85 -> 9.86 -> 11.90 -> 14.88), and the SPCommUpdateCount barrier grows in step (1446 -> 5126 s).
mechanism.reading: Weighting particles does not change how much chemistry work exists; it just relocates cells onto the wrong ranks. Chemistry cost follows CELLS (and per-cell Grackle iteration counts), and it is the dominant imbalance term. Telling the balancer that particle-heavy grids are expensive makes it spread cells to compensate, destroying the cell-based balance that was imperfectly working.

hypotheses_falsified: The audit's T2.1 premise that FOGGIE's imbalance is driven by particle concentration, at least in a simple linear cells+w*particles form.

My own hypothesis (stated before the run) that particle count is a physical proxy for chemistry cost because dense star-forming gas takes the most Grackle iterations. Total chemistry time is flat across weights, so no such useful correlation exists here.
Corroborating prior evidence that should have carried more weight: directly measured particle work is tiny - StarParticleHandler 0.6% of wall, ParticleUpdate 0.02%.

confound_checked.concern: weight>0 also enables an added Allreduce (to agree particle counts across ranks); weight=0 skips it, so the arms differ in two ways.
confound_checked.resolution: Measured separately via RH_PERF loadbal phase: 13 s (w=0) -> 79.6 / 103 / 151 s. The added collective costs ~67 s at w=1 against a +1492 s regression, i.e. ~4%. RebuildHierarchy total 183 -> 213 / 249 / 333 s. The regression is dominated by the barrier (imbalance), not by the added collective.

recommendation: Abandon the linear particle-weighted estimate. The audit's own T2.1 phrasing is 'particle-aware (THEN measured-work)' - go straight to measured-work: use actual per-grid elapsed time from the previous cycle as the weight, which captures chemistry variation, particle work and everything else without guessing a ratio. Enzo already has the plumbing: LoadBalanceHilbertCurve(grid*[], int, float *InputGridWork, int*) accepts externally supplied per-grid work. The code landed here is retained because the parameter defaults to 0 (bit-for-bit historical behaviour) and the rank-agreement Allreduce is a prerequisite for ANY data-dependent weighting, measured-work included.
implication_for_SPFinalize: The 62.9% barrier is NOT reachable by fixing the work estimate this way. audit/SPFinalize_Edits.md remains the largest identified opportunity, and this experiment did not shrink it.

correctness.check: compare_runs w=0 vs w=10, class C0 vs the 3-pair envelope floor
correctness.result: FAIL - DD0397 metal_mass 2.152e-07 vs gate 5.052e-08, baryon_mass 2.346e-08 vs gate 2.303e-08 (marginal).
correctness.reading: Load-balance changes are C1/C2 by nature (they change FP accumulation order via grid ownership), so exceeding a C0 envelope floor is not alarming - but it is larger than the T0.2 Hilbert change produced, which passed C0. Recorded for completeness; the arm is abandoned on performance grounds regardless.
correctness.note: An earlier draft of this file described the arms as answer-neutral before this check completed. That was premature and is corrected here.
